title_en: Checking in: breakfast, wifi and checkout

situation.en: You arrive at your hotel in Chicago, and your reservation is fine. While you check in, you want to know about breakfast, the wifi and checkout time.
situation.he: הגעתם למלון בשיקגו, וההזמנה מסודרת. בזמן הצ'ק-אין אתם רוצים לברר על ארוחת הבוקר, על הוויי-פיי ועל שעת הצ'ק-אאוט.

goal.en: Check in and ask three simple questions: breakfast, the wifi password and checkout time.
goal.he: לעשות צ'ק-אין ולשאול שלוש שאלות פשוטות: על ארוחת הבוקר, על הסיסמה לוויי-פיי ועל שעת הצ'ק-אאוט.

phrases.en: Hi, I'd like to check in. My name is Dana Cohen.
phrases.he: שלום, אשמח לעשות צ'ק-אין. קוראים לי דנה כהן.

phrases.en: Could I have a second key card, please?
phrases.he: אפשר לקבל עוד כרטיס לחדר, בבקשה?

phrases.en: Which floor is my room on?
Could you write it down for me, please?
phrases.he: אפשר לכתוב לי את זה, בבקשה?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Yes, hi. My name is Dana Cohen.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Great, I have you here for two nights. Can I see your ID and a credit card, please?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Sure, here you go. Is breakfast included?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Yes, it is. It's from 6:30 to 10 in the restaurant on the first floor.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Great. And what's the wifi password?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: It's on this card, with your room number. You're in 512, on the fifth floor.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Checkout is at 11. The elevators are on your right. Enjoy your stay!

options.text: Yes, hello. I have a reservation for three nights.

feedback.en: Correct and polite, but the most useful thing is missing: your name. That's the next question anyway.
feedback.he: נכון ומנומס, אבל חסר הדבר הכי שימושי: השם שלכם. זו ממילא השאלה הבאה.

options.text: Yes, I want room for me, for three nights, with a big bed.

feedback.en: 'a' is missing, and 'I want' sounds abrupt. It also sounds as if you have no booking, but your room is already reserved. Say 'Yes, I have a reservation.'
feedback.he: חסר a, ו-I want נשמע ישיר מדי. זה גם נשמע כאילו אין לכם הזמנה, למרות שהחדר כבר שמור לכם. אומרים: Yes, I have a reservation.

options.text: Yes, hi. My name is Dana Cohen.

feedback.en: Short, friendly, and it gives the receptionist what they need.
feedback.he: קצר, ידידותי, ומוסר בדיוק את המידע שצריך בקבלה.

model_replies: Yes, hi. My name is Dana Cohen.
Yes, I have a reservation. My name is Dana Cohen.

practice.partner: Here's your key card. You're in room 512, on the fifth floor.

feedback.en: The word order is wrong. In a question, 'is' comes before 'there', and 'free' goes before 'breakfast': 'Is there free breakfast?' Even simpler: 'Is breakfast included?'
feedback.he: סדר המילים שגוי. בשאלה is בא לפני there, ו-free בא לפני breakfast: Is there free breakfast? ועוד יותר פשוט: Is breakfast included?

feedback.en: A short, natural question. 'Is ... included?' is the standard way to ask.
feedback.he: שאלה קצרה וטבעית. Is ... included? היא הדרך המקובלת לשאול.

feedback.en: Natural, but not very clear: do you mean the time, the place or the price? Ask exactly what you want to know.
feedback.he: טבעי, אבל לא מספיק ברור: השעה, המקום או המחיר? עדיף לשאול בדיוק מה שרוצים לדעת.

model_replies: Thank you. What time is breakfast?

practice.partner: Yes, it is. Breakfast is from 6:30 to 10 in the restaurant.

options.text: Great. And what's the wifi password?

feedback.en: Natural and polite. 'And' connects it nicely to the conversation.
feedback.he: טבעי ומנומס. And מחבר את השאלה יפה לשיחה.

options.text: Give me the wifi password, please.

feedback.en: Even with 'please', it sounds like an order. Ask: 'What's the wifi password?'
feedback.he: גם עם please זה נשמע כמו פקודה. שואלים: What's the wifi password?

options.text: What is the code of the internet?

feedback.en: A word-for-word translation, and it sounds strange. In English we say 'the wifi password'.
feedback.he: תרגום מילה במילה, וזה נשמע מוזר. באנגלית אומרים the wifi password.

model_replies: Great. And what's the wifi password?
Thanks. Is there wifi in the room?

practice.partner: The password is on this card. Anything else?

options.text: When do I need to leave the room?

feedback.en: Correct and clear, but 'What time is checkout?' is what people usually ask.
feedback.he: נכון וברור, אבל בדרך כלל שואלים What time is checkout?

options.text: When I must go out from here?

feedback.en: The word order is wrong, and 'go out' means going out for a while (for example, to have fun), not leaving the hotel. Say 'What time is checkout?'
feedback.he: סדר המילים שגוי, ו-go out פירושו לצאת לזמן מה (למשל לבלות), לא לעזוב את המלון. שואלים: What time is checkout?

feedback.en: The standard hotel question: short and clear.

model_replies: Just one thing: what time is checkout?

roleplay.persona: Marcus, a cheerful receptionist at a big hotel in Chicago. He talks quickly and likes to chat about the city.
roleplay.complication: Breakfast isn't included in the learner's rate; it costs extra. Marcus mentions this quickly, so the learner has to ask him to repeat it and decide whether to add breakfast.
roleplay.opening_line: Hey there, welcome to the Lakeview! Checking in?

culture.en: In the US, the 'first floor' is the ground floor. In the UK, as in Israel, the 'first floor' is one floor up.
culture.he: בארצות הברית first floor היא קומת הקרקע. בבריטניה, כמו בישראל, first floor היא הקומה הראשונה מעל הקרקע.

culture.en: Hotels often ask for a credit card at check-in to cover extras such as room service or the minibar, even if you've already paid for the room.
culture.he: מלונות מבקשים לעיתים קרובות כרטיס אשראי בצ'ק-אין כדי לכסות הוצאות נוספות, כמו שירות חדרים או מיני-בר, גם אם החדר כבר שולם.
